newsitem.title: UK: Enterprise profit up, raises output estimate.
newsitem.headline: Enterprise profit up, raises output estimate.

text.p: Britain's largest independent oil exploration and production company, Enterprise Oil Plc, on Thursday reported a 40 percent increase in its 1996 profits and raised its production forecast for 1999.

Profit after tax rose to 142.5 million pounds ($228.8 million) from 101.6 million pounds, coming in at the low end of analysts' expectations. Enterprise said it expected 1999 production to rise to 320,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day from an average 242,932 in 1996.
Enterprise had previously forecast 1999 production of 300,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day.
The group said 1996 profit was boosted by record production, higher oil prices and tight cost control, while significant discoveries strengthened its reserve base.
"This all represents a reinforcement of our operational base to secure growth and sustained profitabilty over the coming years," chairman Graham Hearne said in a statement.
Enterprise raised its 1996 dividend to 17.0 pence per share from 16.0 pence. Most analysts had expected the pay-out to remain unchanged.
